newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA TELKOM SEES FURTHER GROWTH IN SECOND HALF.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA TELKOM SEES FURTHER GROWTH IN SECOND HALF.

text.p: South Africa's state telecommunications utility Telkom said on Wednesday it expected further growth in the second half of the year but said the slowdown in the economy would weigh on results.

"Telkom anticipates a similar increase in trading profits in the second half of the year, although the apparent slowdown in the economy and the recent rise in interest rates can be expected to impact on results," managing director and chief executive officer Brian Clark said in a statement.

Although Telkom's capital expenditure programme slowed marginally in the first half, the group was committed to a roll out of 250,000 lines, including 30,000 payphones, before financial year-end, Clark said.
This would involve capital expenditure in excess of 3.5 billion rand, a significantly higher commitment than in previous months.

"The company had simultaneously made considerable progress in streamlining procurement procedures, in line with international best practices, with a resulting reduction in inventory and procuremnet costs," Clark said.
He said Telkom's drive to transform itself into a world-class telecommunications company was producing results.
"Re-engineering in particular is bringing about marked improvements in key customer-driven processes such as fault repair and service activation."
Clark said the new Telecommunications Act, passed last month, had given the group a framework which would help it to meet its ambitious roll-out plans and to compete internationally.
However, there were several issues which called for management action.
"In particular, Telkom's local tariffs are presently heavily subsidised by long distance and international calls and...a more balanced a cost-related tariff structure must be implemented".
Clark said he was encouraged by recent steps taken to find a strategic equity partner for the state utility.

"We are encouraged by the progress made by the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Broadcasting and the company in finding a strategic equity partner and look forward to the successful conclusion of this process in the first quarter of 1997," Clark said.
In the longer-term, Telkom expected to continue the transformation of its business and step up the provision of new lines.

South African Minister for Posts and Telecommunications Jay Naidoo at the beginning of November named Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom , Telekom Malaysia and South Western Bell as finalists for a 20 to 30 percent stake in Telkom.
The sale of a stake in Telkom to foreign bidders is the first major step in the South African government's privatisation programme and is seen as a litmus test of its commitment to economic reform.
